_about.one_line: Deterministic dispatch routing, a Rust done-gate that demands physical proof of completion, and research grounding for agent briefs.
_about.quicktest: PYTHONPATH=.:bin python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_dispatch_router.py tests/test_research_setup.py

tests.title: Dispatch router: task classes, dead-lane filtering, low-yield demotion
tests.claim: The router sends work only to live, productive model lanes: classification by task kind and role, dead-lane filtering (local lanes exempt), demotion of lanes with at least 4 attempts and no productive settle in 24 h (DOSSIER).
tests.verify: T=$(mktemp -d); cp -a . "$T/r"; (cd "$T/r"; export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; PYTHONPATH=.:bin python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_dispatch_router.py) > "$T/o" 2>&1; rc=$?; tail -n 3 "$T/o"; grep -q "1 passed" "$T/o" && [ $rc -eq 0 ]; r=$?; rm -rf "$T"; exit $r
tests.what_it_means: On fixture databases the router maps (research, oracle, build) to classes and a build task by an architect to 'judgment'; keeps a free model and an exempt local ollama lane while dropping a dead one; and puts a productive lane ahead of a flaky one. It shows the routing rules do what the DOSSIER says on small fixtures; it does not show the routes are the best ones for your fleet, and the 4-attempt/24 h thresholds are fixed constants.
tests.how_we_got_it: tests/test_dispatch_router.py builds throw-away `dispatch.db` and `lane-catalog.db` with build_fixture_dbs.py (schema in schema.sql), then asserts on task_class, filter_live and demote_low_yield. Run on this laptop on 2026-10-16: 1 passed. The fixtures stand in for the private lane catalogue, which was replaced by a fixture schema at release prep on 09-29.
tests.use_in_your_work: If you route work across free and paid models, the same three steps (classify, drop dead lanes, demote lanes that never finish) are a cheap way to stop wasting calls on models that are down.
tests.honest_limits: Fixture data only; no real provider status is consulted.

tests.title: Research grounding: sources checked on disk, missing target blocks the dispatch
tests.claim: Research grounding appends a `## RESEARCH GROUNDING (auto)` block listing found and missing sources, and returns an error if the brief's target is missing (DOSSIER).
tests.verify: T=$(mktemp -d); cp -a . "$T/r"; (cd "$T/r"; export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; PYTHONPATH=.:bin python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_research_setup.py) > "$T/o" 2>&1; rc=$?; tail -n 3 "$T/o"; grep -q "1 passed" "$T/o" && [ $rc -eq 0 ]; r=$?; rm -rf "$T"; exit $r
tests.what_it_means: A brief that names a real source file and a missing file gets the real one listed as found and the missing one listed as missing, the grounding marker is appended, and a brief whose target does not exist returns an error. It proves the check reads the disk rather than trusting the brief; it checks paths exist, not that their content is relevant.
tests.how_we_got_it: tests/test_research_setup.py, standalone mode (`ARK_NO_NOTEBOOK=1`), in a temp directory. Run on this laptop on 2026-10-16: 1 passed.
tests.use_in_your_work: Before you hand a long task to an agent, check that every file the brief names exists. It is a tiny script that prevents a whole class of wasted runs.
tests.honest_limits: Only existence of paths is checked; the notebook mode is not exercised.

tests.title: Done-gate behavioural suite: 11 real-binary verdict cases
tests.claim: The Rust done-gate refuses to call a task finished unless its named deliverable exists, is non-empty and was produced during the task, or a passing `--gate-cmd` proves it; every named path must pass; exit 0 VERIFIED, 1 UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED, 2 NOCLAIM (DOSSIER). 11 behavioural cases against the real binary.
tests.verify: T=$(mktemp -d); cp -a . "$T/r"; (cd "$T/r"; export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_done_gate_behaviour.py) | tail -n 3; rm -rf "$T"
tests.what_it_means: Fresh deliverable is VERIFIED; missing, stale (older than the dispatch start) and empty deliverables are UNVERIFIED; a passing gate command carries a path-less claim and a failing one refuses; an unverifiable claim is refused; BLOCKED and no-claim-yet get their own verdicts; with several named paths all must pass. This is the 'physical proof' claim as executable cases. It does not show an agent cannot fake the file itself: a file that exists, is fresh and non-empty passes.
tests.how_we_got_it: tests/test_done_gate_behaviour.py builds a workspace with `control-center/dispatch.db` (schema.sql), a dispatch log and optionally a deliverable, builds the binary with `cargo build --offline` and runs it. Not run for this record (needs cargo). A trial run of the whole suite in a temporary copy on this laptop on 2026-10-16 printed `14 passed in 8.56s`; the DOSSIER records 14/14 (3 unit groups + 11 behavioural cases) on 2026-10-01.
tests.use_in_your_work: Add the same check to any pipeline where an agent says 'done': require a named file newer than the task start, or a command that exits 0.
tests.honest_limits: Needs the Rust toolchain; the gate shells out to sqlite3 and quotes (does not parameterise) task ids (DOSSIER Limits); `done-gate --selftest` is fleet-specific and not meaningful outside it.

tests.title: Rust unit test and the Python wrapper around cargo test
tests.claim: `make test` also runs `cargo test --offline` in rust-done-gate (release-scan: 'pytest 3 passed; cargo test 1 passed (4/4 passed)' at 2026-09-29).
tests.verify: T=$(mktemp -d); cp -a . "$T/r"; (cd "$T/r"; export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_done_gate.py; cd rust-done-gate && cargo test --offline) 2>&1 | tail -n 5; rm -rf "$T"
tests.expect: 1 passed (pytest wrapper) and test result: ok. 1 passed (cargo)
tests.what_it_means: The single Rust unit test (`test_done_gate_help`) and the pytest wrapper pass, meaning the binary builds offline and answers --help. This is a build-sanity check, not a behavioural one; ARK3 holds the behaviour.
tests.how_we_got_it: rust-done-gate/tests/test_unit.rs and tests/test_done_gate.py; the 2026-09-29 count (3 pytest + 1 cargo) is recorded in release-scan.txt; later counts are in the DOSSIER (14/14 on 2026-10-01). Not run for this record because it needs cargo.
tests.use_in_your_work: Treat it as the smoke test after a rebuild of the gate binary.
tests.honest_limits: Weak on its own: it checks only that the binary starts.

tests.title: Recorded gate latency and fleet usage figures
tests.claim: 'Gate wall time, release build: median 12.2 ms, p90 21.6 ms (50 runs, incl. SQLite lookups)'; 'Fleet dispatches recorded 1,175; tasks ratified done through the gate 883, 462 (52%) with hashed deliverable rows; dispatches settled to review instead of done 86' (DOSSIER).
tests.verify: grep -q 'median 12.2 ms, p90 21.6 ms (50 runs' DOSSIER.md && grep -q 'Fleet dispatches recorded | 1,175' DOSSIER.md && grep -q '883; 462 (52%)' DOSSIER.md && grep -q 'review instead of done | 86' DOSSIER.md && echo 'recorded: 12.2 ms / 21.6 ms, 1,175, 883, 462 (52%), 86'
tests.what_it_means: The DOSSIER states a typical gate latency of a few tens of milliseconds and fleet usage counts. Passing here proves only that these figures are written in the committed DOSSIER. The latency test in the suite (`test_latency`) asserts only a loose bound of under 1000 ms median; the 12.2/21.6 ms figures are a release build measured separately. The usage counts come from the author's private fleet database, which is not in the repo.
tests.how_we_got_it: Latency: 50 runs of the release build including SQLite lookups, 'this repo' per the DOSSIER (machine and date not recorded beyond the DOSSIER's 2026-10-01 test line). Usage counts: 'fleet DB, verified 10-01'.
tests.use_in_your_work: A feel for cost: the gate is cheap enough to run on every completion.
tests.honest_limits: Not reproducible from the repo: the fleet DB and the 50-run harness are not shipped. In the DOSSIER the 52% means 462 of 883 ratified tasks had hashed deliverable rows, i.e. 48% were not gated on a hashed file.

tests.title: Release scan: no leaks, no home paths, nothing vendored
tests.claim: gitleaks 8.24.0: no leaks found; home-directory paths of the development machine: 0; vendored third-party binaries/sources: none (release-scan.txt).
tests.verify: grep -q 'no leaks found' release-scan.txt && grep -q 'machine (grep -rn over the tree): 0' release-scan.txt && ! grep -rIl --exclude-dir=.git --exclude=release-scan.txt -E '/home/[a-z]+/' . && echo 'scan recorded; no /home/<user>/ path in the tree'
tests.expect: scan recorded; no /home/<user>/ path in the tree
tests.what_it_means: The committed scan says no secrets and no developer paths and the path grep is re-run on the clone. gitleaks itself is not re-run.
tests.how_we_got_it: release-scan.txt, gitleaks 8.24.0 `detect --no-git -s . --redact`, at release prep (the `make test` line in it is dated 2026-09-29).
tests.use_in_your_work: Before publishing your own agent tooling, run the same two checks.
tests.honest_limits: Only the grep is re-run here.
